Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
240 PM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 239 PM EDT Wednesday...

No significant changes

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 239 PM EDT Wednesday...

1. Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.

2. Mostly dry and seasonable conditions continue through the 
weekend. 

3. Seasonable and mainly dry weather will continue through 
at least the first half of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 239 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: While conditions are not expected to reach Red Flag 
Criteria in the upcoming future, gusty conditions and lower relative 
humidity values will cause increased fire weather concerns due to 
plentiful dry leaves on the ground serving as fuel. Winds gusts 
tomorrow and Friday are generally expected to be in the 15 to 25 mph 
range, with some gusts up to 30 mph possible. The highest gusts are 
expected in the St. Lawrence Valley and northern slopes of the 
Adirondacks where gusts up to 35 mph are possible tomorrow. Relative 
humidity values will generally be in the 40-55 percent range 
tomorrow. Relative humidity values are expected in that range again 
on Friday for most places, but localized drops into the 30-40 
percent range are possible in the Lower Connecticut River Valley. 
Heading into the weekend, winds will mostly remain under 15 mph. 
However, relative humidity values should drop into the 30-45 percent 
range for most places, with a localized drop into upper 20s possible 
in the Lower Connecticut Valley. A few showers are possible tomorrow 
evening and overnight, but a wetting rain is not expected anywhere.

KEY MESSAGE 2: After a warm day tomorrow, a cold front comes through 
tomorrow night and into early Friday. A few showers are possible 
across northern New York and the higher elevations of northern 
Vermont but with dry air aloft and weak forcing, they will be brief 
and only lead to a couple hundreths of an inch of rain locally. The 
highest amounts are expected in the northern Greens and the 
Adirondacks. Strong cold air advection will occur on Friday with 
clouds in the typical upslope areas. Surface high pressure builds 
overhead into the weekend, leading to mostly sunny skies and 
moderating temperatures. The Halloween forecast looks great with 
clear skies, light winds and temperatures quickly dropping from the 
50s into the 30s during the evening. However, despite clear skies, 
any added ambiance from the moon will mostly be missing as it was 
full a couple days ago and will rise around 10:45 Halloween evening.

KEY MESSAGE 3: While no hazardous weather is expected, there is some 
disagreement amongst ensemble guidance on the upper level pattern 
early next week. The consensus idea amongst non-GEFS guidance 
strongly favors a more amplified ridge to our west maintaining 
northwest flow over our region and deflecting most precipitation 
well to our west. In this most likely scenario, low level 
temperatures remain above normal with near surface winds primarily 
out of the south and chances of rain are very low. 

While certainly not indicating any significant weather, the majority 
of GEFS membership in contrast suggests some weak troughing that 
allows a shortwave to push showers in from the west. As such, this 
less likely scenario brings rainfall chances closer to 60% to 75% in 
the Monday afternoon through Tuesday timeframe, and for amounts 
exceeding 0.25" mainly 20-30%, or slightly higher in the 
Adirondacks. 

Finally, there are indications that a weak surface cold front 
similar to ones we've seen in recent weeks could slip in from the 
north. It would bring chances for very light rain and a cloudier 
period with reinforcement of seasonably cool air. This complicates 
the temperature forecast for Tuesday, when the high temperature 
forecast is relatively uncertain compared to Monday (about twice the 
model spread).

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 18Z Thursday...No hazardous conditions expected during the
period at terminals. VFR will prevail along, while typical terrain-
driven flow increases somewhat overnight as high pressure slides to
our southeast. Despite clearing skies, fog probabilities are low
especially due to the southwesterly flow off the deck. Would not
rule out perhaps brief intervals near 10Z at MPV, but chances are
under 10%. From 14Z to 18Z, terminals in the wide valleys (MSS, PBG,
BTV) will see gusty south/southwest winds develop under full
sunshine/effective mixing and channeling. Relatively modest gust
magnitudes could peak as high as 25 to 30 knots.

Outlook...

Thursday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.EQUIPMENT...
Routine observations from KSLK ASOS are unavailable until
further notice. While the site is operating, it is not able to
disseminate observations normally at this time. Technicians are
aware of the issue, but time of return to service is unknown.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
